rationales: Air is generally a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Rock is heterogeneous because its components are not uniformly distributed.
Gasoline is generally a homogeneous mixture of hydrocarbons.
Ice cream is a colloid and is also classified as a heterogeneous mixture, so the question has more than one correct option.
HO is not the empirical formula of glucose.
CH does not give the simplest whole-number ratio of glucose atoms.
CH₂O is the empirical formula obtained by simplifying C₆H₁₂O₆.
H₂O₂ is not the empirical formula of glucose.
C-12 is a stable isotope and is not used for cancer treatment.
C-14 is primarily used for radiocarbon dating.
P-32 is a radioactive isotope used in some cancer treatments, including treatment of skin cancer.
I-131 is principally used to diagnose and treat thyroid disorders.
The 2nd and 3rd periods are called short periods.
Normal periods refers to the 4th and 5th periods.
Long periods refers to the 6th and 7th periods in this classification.
Very long periods is not the name for the 2nd and 3rd periods.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs.
Donation of electrons alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
Acceptance of electrons alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
Repulsion of electrons does not form a covalent bond.
CH₄ is nonpolar and is poorly soluble in water.
C₂H₂ is largely nonpolar and is poorly soluble in water.
NaCl is ionic and dissolves readily in water.
C₆H₆ is nonpolar and does not dissolve appreciably in water.
Manufacturing sulphuric acid is an application of industrial chemistry.
Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms.
Organic chemistry primarily studies carbon compounds.
Inorganic chemistry studies inorganic substances, but industrial manufacture is classified as industrial chemistry.
Sugar is a compound, not a mixture.
Pure water is a compound, not a mixture.
Oxygen is an element, not a mixture.
Air is a mixture of gases.
Deuterium has mass number 2 and one proton, so it does not have zero neutrons.
Deuterium has one neutron because 2 − 1 = 1.
Deuterium has only one neutron, not two.
Deuterium has only one neutron, not three.
Li has a larger atomic radius than the elements farther across its period.
Be has a larger atomic radius than F.
Ne is a noble gas, whose tabulated van der Waals radius is not the smallest among these choices.
Across the period, atomic radius decreases toward F, making F the expected smallest here.
NaNO₃ becomes more soluble as temperature increases.
Li₂SO₄ solubility does not show the strong increase expected for this answer.
Ce₂(SO₄)₃ becomes less soluble with increasing temperature.
NaCl solubility changes only slightly with temperature.
Polar covalent compounds commonly dissolve in polar water.
Benzene is nonpolar and generally dissolves nonpolar substances.
Ether is less suitable than water as a general solvent for polar compounds.
Acetone is polar, but water is the expected solvent for polar covalent compounds in this question.
NaCl has an ionic bond, not a coordinate covalent bond.
In NH₄Cl, the ammonium ion forms when nitrogen donates a lone pair to H⁺, creating a coordinate bond.
H₂O has ordinary covalent O–H bonds.
NH₃ has ordinary covalent N–H bonds and a lone pair, but no coordinate bond within the molecule.
C₁₀H₂₂ has a higher boiling point and evaporates more slowly than the shorter alkanes listed.
C₉H₂₀ evaporates more slowly than the shorter-chain choices.
C₈H₁₈ evaporates more slowly than C₆H₁₄.
C₆H₁₄ has the shortest chain and weakest intermolecular attractions here, so it evaporates most rapidly.
15.2°C is not the transition temperature of tin.
14.2°C is not the transition temperature of tin.
Tin’s transition temperature is approximately 13.2°C.
12.2°C is not the transition temperature of tin.
